# Superlog documentation

Source for [docs.superlog.sh](https://docs.superlog.sh), built with [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com).

Superlog automates routine engineering tasks: it triages alerts, answers support questions, and reviews performance and observability in your code and infrastructure. The application code is at [superloglabs/responder-oss](https://github.com/superloglabs/responder-oss).

## Preview locally

```bash
npm i -g mint
mint dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

## Check links

```bash
mint broken-links
```

## Publish

Changes deploy automatically after they are merged to `main`.

---
title: "Security"
description: "How Superlog protects credentials, isolates runs, and limits what agents can access."
---

Superlog gives agents useful access to your tools without handing them your keys. This page summarizes the controls. For more detail, read the [security whitepaper](https://superlog.sh/security).

## Credentials stay outside the sandbox

Agents run in sandboxes that do not hold your provider credentials.

| Credential | How agents use it |
|---|---|
| GitHub | Superlog copies repositories into the sandbox and opens pull requests on the agent's behalf. The sandbox has no GitHub token. |
| Integrations | Superlog calls Slack, Sentry, Datadog, Linear, and MCP servers for the agent through a broker outside the sandbox. |
| Model API keys | Model requests go through a broker that holds the key. Keys never enter the sandbox. |
| ChatGPT subscription | Each run gets a copy of the login with placeholder tokens. The real access token is substituted at the network boundary, only for requests to ChatGPT. |
| Workspace secrets | The sandbox gets a placeholder. The real value is substituted at the network boundary, only for allowed hosts. |

## Encryption

- Integration tokens and API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before storage, with a fresh random nonce for each encryption.
- Database storage and application logs use managed encryption keys with rotation enabled.
- Public traffic and database connections require TLS.

## Short-lived cloud access

- AWS uses temporary credentials from an IAM role in your account. An explicit deny blocks secrets, SSM parameters, and KMS decryption.
- Google Cloud uses Workload Identity Federation. No service account key is created or stored.
- The roles you create define the access boundary.

## Isolated runs

- Every automation, integration, secret, run, and member belongs to one workspace. Queries and API routes enforce that ownership.
- Each run gets its own sandbox. Sandboxes are never shared across workspaces.
- Each run keeps the exact automation configuration it started with.

## Limited tools

- Most built-in integrations expose only read-only tools. Write actions are limited to opening pull requests, posting to Slack, and creating Linear issues.
- Datadog and custom MCP servers pass their tools through. Scope the credentials you give them.
- Custom MCP servers must use HTTPS and resolve to public addresses. Authorization is never forwarded across origins.
- Agents treat trigger events as untrusted input.

## Webhooks

Slack, GitHub, Sentry, and Discord webhooks are verified against their signatures before Superlog acts on them. Retries are deduplicated.

## Report a vulnerability

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/superloglabs/responder-oss/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability privately.

> For Mintlify product knowledge (components, configuration, writing standards),
> install the Mintlify skill: `npx skills add https://mintlify.com/docs`

# Documentation project instructions

## About this project

- This is a documentation site built on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com)
- Pages are MDX files with YAML frontmatter
- Configuration lives in `docs.json`
- Use the Mintlify MCP server, `https://mcp.mintlify.com`, to edit content and settings via MCP
- Use the Mintlify docs MCP server, `https://www.mintlify.com/docs/mcp`, to query information about using Mintlify via MCP

## Terminology

- The product is **Superlog**. The open-source repository is `superloglabs/responder-oss`; use the name Responder only when referring to that repository or to identifiers in it.
- An **automation** has **triggers**, **agent instructions**, **repositories**, **connectors**, a **model**, and a **harness**. One execution is a **run**.
- **Tag mode** answers Slack mentions. It is separate from automations.
- Use "workspace" for the tenant and "integration" for a connected tool.
- Positioning follows the landing page at superlog.sh: automate routine engineering tasks; choose your model and harness; bring your own tokens and subscriptions.

## Style preferences

- Plain, direct language. Short sentences. No marketing flourish.
- Use active voice and second person ("you")
- Keep sentences concise — one idea per sentence
- Use sentence case for headings
- Bold for UI elements: Click **Settings**
- Code formatting for file names, commands, paths, and code references

## Content boundaries

- Document what the current code does. Check claims against `superloglabs/responder-oss` before publishing.
- Document the automations product that hosted workspaces get. Do not document internal admin features.

---
title: "Management API"
sidebarTitle: "Introduction"
description: "Manage automations, runs, tag mode, model access, and secrets over HTTP."
---

The management API lets scripts, CI jobs, and agents do what you do in **Settings**, **Automations**, and **Tag mode**: create and change automations, start and follow runs, change tag mode, and manage model keys and workspace secrets.

The same operations are available as tools in the [Superlog MCP server](/api-reference/mcp).

## Base URL

```text
https://superlog.sh/api/v1
```

A self-hosted deployment serves the API at `/api/v1` on its own origin.

## Authentication

Send a workspace API key as a bearer token:

```bash
curl https://superlog.sh/api/v1/workspace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPERLOG_API_KEY"
```

Create keys under **Settings → API keys**. See [API keys](/settings/api-keys).

A key belongs to one workspace and acts as the member who created it. Changes made with the key are recorded under that member's name. The key stops working when it is revoked or when that member leaves the workspace.

## Find the IDs you need

Automations and tag mode refer to repositories, integrations, channels, and secrets by ID. Look them up first:

- `GET /integrations` returns connected integrations, the repositories GitHub gives access to, and integration resources such as Slack channels and Sentry projects.
- `GET /secrets` returns workspace secrets.

Integrations are connected in the app. After you give the GitHub App access to a new repository or create a Slack channel, call `POST /integrations/refresh` to load it.

## Create an automation

```bash
curl https://superlog.sh/api/v1/automations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPERLOG_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Weekly dependency review",
    "configuration": {
      "prompt": "Review outdated dependencies and open a pull request for safe upgrades.",
      "repositoryIds": ["f458cf4e-7e6f-452c-8da6-3187a35c1f10"],
      "triggers": [
        { "kind": "schedule", "frequency": "weekly", "hour": 9, "weekday": 1, "timezone": "Europe/Paris" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

Model settings you leave out use the defaults: the Codex harness with `gpt-5.4`. See [Models and harnesses](/automations/models).

## Change part of an automation

`PATCH` requests change only the fields you send. In `configuration`, each field you send replaces the current value, and a list you send replaces the whole list.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://superlog.sh/api/v1/automations/$AUTOMATION_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPERLOG_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "configuration": { "prompt": "Also check for security advisories." } }'
```

Send only `enabled` to turn an automation on or off. `PATCH /tag-mode` works the same way.

## Start and follow a run

`POST /automations/{automationId}/runs` starts a run and returns its `runId`. Add a `message` to start the run as a chat. Poll `GET /runs/{runId}` until `status` is `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. `resultSummary` holds the agent's final answer, and `events` holds the transcript.

Send a follow-up with `POST /runs/{runId}/messages` once the run has finished.

## Errors

Errors return a JSON body with a message and, when there is one, a stable `code`:

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "error": "Invalid request",
  "issues": [{ "message": "Invalid UUID", "path": ["automationId"] }]
}
```

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | The request is invalid. `issues` lists each invalid field. |
| `401` | The API key is missing, revoked, or its member left the workspace. |
| `404` | The resource is not in this workspace, or automations are not enabled for it. |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state, such as a name already in use or a run that is still active. |
| `502`, `503` | A provider or the run queue is unavailable. Try again. |

## What stays in the app

Connecting integrations, inviting and removing members, billing, creating API keys, and connecting a ChatGPT subscription are done in the app.

---
title: "Models and harnesses"
sidebarTitle: "Models and harnesses"
description: "Choose any model and agent harness for each automation, and run on your own API keys or ChatGPT subscription."
---

Each automation picks its own model and harness. You can switch providers without rebuilding your automations, and you can run on your own API keys or your ChatGPT subscription instead of the usage included in your plan.

## Choose a model

In the automation editor, click **Choose model** in the **Agent instructions** toolbar. Pick a provider, then a model from its list.

| Provider | Harnesses |
|---|---|
| OpenAI | Codex, OpenCode |
| Anthropic | Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode |
| Google Gemini | OpenCode |
| xAI | OpenCode |
| Mistral | OpenCode |
| DeepSeek | OpenCode |

Model lists are loaded from each provider's current catalog. The provider decides at run time whether a model is available to your key.

## Choose a harness

The harness is the agent program that runs the model in the sandbox. When you pick a model, Superlog switches to a compatible harness: Codex for OpenAI, the Claude Agent SDK (shown as **Anthropic**) for Anthropic, and OpenCode for the others. Click **Harness** to change it.

| Harness | Providers |
|---|---|
| **Codex** | OpenAI. Required to use a ChatGPT subscription. |
| **Anthropic** (Claude Agent SDK) | Anthropic |
| **OpenCode** | All six providers |

All harnesses run unattended, without approval prompts.

## Where inference comes from

Superlog picks the inference source when each run starts:

1. **ChatGPT subscription**, if one is connected and the automation uses the Codex harness.
2. **Your API key** for the model's provider. With several keys for one provider, the newest is used.
3. **Included usage** from your plan, if neither of the above applies.

If the provider rejects your key, or your key cannot use the selected model, the run fails with a message that names the problem. It does not fall back to included usage.

## Add an API key

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open model settings">
    Go to **Settings → Models**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add the key">
    Under **Add an API key**, choose the provider, enter a label, and paste the key. Click **Add key**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check the result">
    Superlog checks the key against the provider's model list before saving it. The key appears under **API keys** with its label, provider, last four characters, and status.
  </Step>
</Steps>

From then on, every automation that uses that provider runs on your key, and your provider bills the model usage. Keys are encrypted and never enter the automation sandbox. Click **Replace** to rotate a key, or **Remove** to delete it. A key that an automation is using cannot be removed.

## Connect a ChatGPT subscription

Automations that use the Codex harness can run on a ChatGPT plan. The subscription takes priority over any OpenAI API key, and usage counts against that plan's Codex limits.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Start the sign-in">
    Go to **Settings → Models**, click **Connect ChatGPT**, then **Connect subscription**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enter the code">
    Superlog shows a one-time code. Click **Continue to ChatGPT**, sign in, and enter the code. If ChatGPT asks, enable device-code login in your ChatGPT security settings.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Finish">
    When the sign-in completes, the subscription appears with **Codex harness only**. Every automation in the workspace can use it.
  </Step>
</Steps>

If the subscription stops working, it shows **Reconnect**. Sign in again to restore it.

<Note>
  Superlog uses OpenAI's official Codex client for sign-in and inference. Your tokens are encrypted, and each run's sandbox holds only placeholders that are replaced at the network boundary. Anthropic subscription sign-in is not available.
</Note>

---
title: "API keys"
description: "Create keys for the management API and the MCP server."
---

API keys give the [management API](/api-reference/introduction) and the [MCP server](/api-reference/mcp) access to one workspace. With a key, they can read and change automations, runs, tag mode, model access, and workspace secrets.

## How keys work

- A key acts as the member who created it. Changes made with it are recorded under that member's name.
- A key stops working when it is revoked or when its member leaves the workspace.
- Superlog stores only a hash of the key. You can see the full key once, right after you create it.

## Create a key

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open API keys">
    Go to **Settings → API keys**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Name the key">
    Under **Create an API key**, enter a name that says where the key is used, such as `Claude Code` or `CI`, and click **Create key**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Copy the key">
    Click **Copy key** and store it in your secret manager or MCP client. Keys start with `slk_`.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Revoke a key

Click **Revoke** next to the key. Anything that uses it stops working immediately.

Members can revoke the keys they created. Admins and owners can revoke any key in the workspace.

The **API keys** list shows the first characters of each key, the member it acts as, and when it was last used.

---
title: "MCP server"
description: "Let Claude, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients manage your Superlog workspace."
---

The Superlog MCP server gives an AI assistant the [management API](/api-reference/introduction) as tools. Ask it to create an automation, change tag mode, start a run, or check why a run failed.

## Server details

| | |
|---|---|
| URL | `https://superlog.sh/api/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth sign-in, or `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` |

Clients that support MCP OAuth sign you in through Superlog. You choose a workspace and approve access, and the assistant acts as you in that workspace.

For clients without OAuth, create an API key under **Settings → API keys** and send it as a bearer token. See [API keys](/settings/api-keys). The assistant acts as the member who created the key.

## Connect a client

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Claude Code">
    Install the Superlog plugin, then run `/mcp` and sign in:

    ```bash
    claude plugin marketplace add superloglabs/claude-plugin
    claude plugin install superlog@superlog
    ```

    See [Claude](/assistants/claude) for the Claude apps and other options.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Cursor">
    Add the server to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "superlog": {
          "url": "https://superlog.sh/api/mcp",
          "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer slk_..." }
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Codex">
    Add the server to `~/.codex/config.toml` and set `SUPERLOG_API_KEY` in your environment:

    ```toml
    [mcp_servers.superlog]
    url = "https://superlog.sh/api/mcp"
    bearer_token_env_var = "SUPERLOG_API_KEY"
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="VS Code">
    Add the server to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks for the key the first time it starts the server:

    ```json
    {
      "inputs": [
        { "type": "promptString", "id": "superlog-key", "description": "Superlog API key", "password": true }
      ],
      "servers": {
        "superlog": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://superlog.sh/api/mcp",
          "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:superlog-key}" }
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Tools

| Area | Tools |
|---|---|
| Workspace | `get_workspace`, `list_members` |
| Integrations | `list_available_integrations`, `start_integration_connection`, `list_integrations`, `refresh_integrations`, `list_sentry_environments` |
| Automations | `list_automations`, `get_automation`, `create_automation`, `update_automation` |
| Runs | `list_automation_runs`, `start_automation_run`, `get_automation_run`, `cancel_automation_run`, `send_automation_run_message` |
| Tag mode | `get_tag_mode`, `update_tag_mode` |
| Models | `list_included_models`, `list_model_credentials`, `list_model_credential_models`, `test_model_credential`, `delete_model_credential` |
| Secrets | `list_secrets` |
| API keys | `list_api_keys`, `revoke_api_key` |

Each tool takes the same fields as its API endpoint. Read-only tools are marked as read-only. `update_automation`, `cancel_automation_run`, `update_tag_mode`, `revoke_api_key`, and `delete_model_credential` are marked as destructive, so clients can ask before running them.

`start_integration_connection` returns a consent link for the person to open in their browser. Integrations that need a credential return a secure setup link instead, so the credential is entered in Superlog and not in the conversation.

Adding a workspace secret or a model API key is not available as a tool, so those values never pass through a model. Use the app or the [API](/api-reference/introduction) for them.

## Example requests

- "Create an automation that reviews new Sentry regressions in the `api` project and opens a pull request in `acme/api`."
- "Turn off the weekly dependency review."
- "Why did the last run of the triage automation fail?"
- "Let tag mode read the `acme/web` repository."

---
title: "Custom MCP servers"
sidebarTitle: "Custom MCP"
description: "Connect any remote MCP server so automations and tag mode can use its tools."
---

Connect your own remote MCP server to give agents tools Superlog does not have built in, such as an internal admin API or a data source you host.

## Requirements

- The server uses the Streamable HTTP transport.
- The URL uses HTTPS and resolves to a public address.
- Authentication is an API token, or OAuth 2.0 with authorization-server discovery, PKCE, and dynamic client registration.

## Add a server

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the dialog">
    In **Integrations**, click **Add** on **Custom MCP**. Or, in the automation connector picker, click **Add custom MCP server**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Enter the server details">
    Enter a **Name** and the **Streamable HTTP URL**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Choose authentication">
    Choose **API token** and paste the token, or choose **OAuth 2.0** and click **Continue with OAuth** to approve access on your server.
  </Step>
</Steps>

For OAuth, Superlog registers a client on your server with this redirect URL:

```text
https://superlog.sh/api/integrations/custom_mcp/callback
```

On a self-hosted deployment, use your own public URL instead.

## Tool access

Superlog passes every tool the server exposes to the agent. It does not filter them to read-only, so the agent can call write tools if the server has them. Expose only the tools you want agents to use, and write clear tool descriptions so the agent knows when to call them.

Your server receives every call the agent makes. Use its logs to audit what agents did.

Redirects are checked again before they are followed, and authorization is never forwarded to another origin.

---
title: "Deploy Superlog"
sidebarTitle: "Deployment"
description: "Deploy the Superlog control plane and worker on your own infrastructure."
---

You run two long-running services, the **control plane** and the **worker**, backed by one Postgres database. Both ship with Dockerfiles you can use as starting points. The application does not depend on a specific cloud provider.

Both services need the same `DATABASE_URL`, `CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `INTERNAL_INGEST_TOKEN`.

<Warning>
  You are responsible for TLS termination, network isolation, database backups, secret injection, monitoring, scaling, and rollbacks.
</Warning>

## Deploy

<Steps>
  <Step title="Build the control plane">
    ```bash
    docker build -f apps/control-plane/Dockerfile -t superlog-control-plane .
    ```

    The Dockerfile is a generic building block. Adapt the networking, base image, and build arguments to your platform.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Serve the app and API from one origin">
    Serve the built assets in `apps/control-plane/dist` at your public origin, and route `/api/*` on the same origin to the control-plane service. Sign-in, OAuth callbacks, and webhooks all depend on one stable origin.

    ```text
    https://superlog.example.com/        → static assets
    https://superlog.example.com/api/*   → control-plane service
    ```

    Set `BETTER_AUTH_URL` to this origin. Set `RESPONDER_PUBLIC_URL` too if integration callbacks and webhooks should use a different public origin. OAuth redirect URIs and webhook URLs are derived from it.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Run the worker">
    ```bash
    docker build -f apps/worker/Dockerfile -t superlog-worker .
    ```

    The worker serves no public traffic. It needs outbound access to the database, Daytona, model providers, and connected integrations.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Apply migrations">
    Before each release starts, apply every migration in `drizzle/`:

    ```bash
    pnpm db:migrate
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Turn on automations">
    Set `RESPONDER_NEW_ORGANIZATION_CAPABILITIES=automations,simplified_navigation` on the control plane so new workspaces get the automations product. See [Self-hosting overview](/self-hosting/overview#turn-on-automations).
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
  Changing the public origin after integrations are connected breaks their OAuth callbacks and webhooks. Update the redirect and webhook URLs in each provider app if you change it.
</Warning>

## Required configuration

| Variable | Service | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Both | Postgres connection string. |
| `CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Both | Base64-encoded 32-byte key that encrypts stored credentials. Must match on both services. |
| `INTERNAL_INGEST_TOKEN` | Both | Shared token for internal requests. Must match on both services. |
| `DAYTONA_API_KEY` | Both | Sandboxes for runs, and the vault for workspace secrets. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Control plane | Signs sign-in sessions. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | Control plane | Public origin of the app. |
| `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | Both | Included usage for automations. Optional if every workspace brings its own key or subscription. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Worker | Tag mode. |

Generate the encryption key and internal token with:

```bash
openssl rand -base64 32   # CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY
openssl rand -hex 32      # INTERNAL_INGEST_TOKEN
```

See [Environment variables](/self-hosting/environment) for every option.

## After deployment

Create provider apps for the integrations you want. Each integration page lists the required callback URLs, webhooks, and permissions. Integrations whose provider app is not configured show **Unavailable** in the app.

---
title: "Plans and billing"
sidebarTitle: "Plans and billing"
description: "Superlog plans, what counts toward your usage quota, and what happens when you reach it."
---

Superlog plans differ by usage quota. Start free and move up as your automations grow. See current prices on the [pricing page](https://superlog.sh/pricing).

| Plan | Price | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0 / month | Teams getting started. A light usage quota, no card required. |
| **Pro** | $100 / month | Teams running automations daily. |
| **Max** | $200 / month | Teams with the highest demand. |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Organizations that need a custom quota, terms, and support. [Talk to us](https://cal.com/superlog/yc). |

## What counts toward your quota

Two things:

- **AI inference** that runs on Superlog's included usage. Runs that use your own API key or ChatGPT subscription are billed by your provider and do not count here.
- **Sandbox compute**, the time each run's sandbox is running. This counts for every run, including runs on your own key.

Automation runs and tag mode questions both draw on the quota.

## Check your usage

Go to **Settings → Billing**. The **Included usage this month** card shows how much of the quota you have used, split into AI inference and sandbox compute, and when it resets.

## When you reach your quota

A banner appears in the app and Superlog sends a notice to Slack. Work that is already running finishes. New runs and tag mode questions do not start until the quota resets at the start of the next billing period or you upgrade.

## Change plans

In **Settings → Billing**, choose a plan:

- **Upgrades** take effect immediately. Superlog charges the saved card for the prorated difference after you confirm.
- **Downgrades** and returning to Free take effect at the end of the current billing period.

Click **Manage billing** to update your payment method or see invoices.
